To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 6‐D‐hydroxy‐nicotine oxidases (6‐HDNO) and the 6‐hydroxynicotine‐oxidase‐reductase (6‐HDNOR) are encoded by a single operon, and that the 6 ‐HDNO gene is negatively regulated by a repressor protein, NicR1.

the catabolic plasmit pAO1 of A. oxidans encodes the repressor of the 6 ‐hydroxy‐D ‐nicotine oxidase (6‐HDNO) gene and that this gene is regulated by the presence of the repressor in a non‐cooperative manner.
the 6‐hydroxylase‐encoding gene is regulated by a repressor, the regulatory protein Nic R1, which interacts with the palindromically arranged promoter region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the NicR1 regulatory protein with the 6HDNO promoter region of Arthrobacter nicotinovorans.
the identification of the regulatory protein and the promoter region of pAO1‐ encoded 6‐HDN oxidase gene, which is the first enzyme of nicotine catabolism.
the interaction of the regulatory protein of the pAO‐1‐encoded 5‐ and 6‐HDN oxidases with the promoter regions of the respective genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NicR1 acts as a positive regulator of 6‐HDN oxidase gene expression in Arthrobacter oxidan s.
NicR1 is a repressor of the 6 ‐HDNO gene, which is not activated by the presence of nicotine.
the regulatory protein Nic R1 binds to the 6HDNO promoter in vitro and in vivo and represses the transcription of the 6HDN O gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NicR1 is a repressor protein that binds to the 6 HDNO promoter and prevents transcription initiation by the E. coli σ70 RNA‐polymerases in vitro.
the binding of NicR1 is independent of the growth stage of the cells and of the presence of its inducer.
the binding of NicR1 in vitro to the 6HDNO promoter region does not correlate with the repression of 6‐HDN O gene expression in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast to the situation in other bacteria where the regulatory protein is induced upon exposure of the cell to the catabolic substrates, the presence of the regulatory protein in A. oxidans is constitutive and independent of the catabolite.

the regulatory protein Nic R1, which is encoded by the catabolic plsmid pAO1 of the Gram‐negative soil bacterium Arthbacter oxidans, interacts with the promoter region and the interpalindomic region of the gene encoding the 6‐hydroxynicotine oxidase (6‐HDNO) enzyme, the first enzyme in the catabolism pathway of the alkaloid nicotine.
the regulatory protein Nicr1 is a DNA‐binding protein that acts as a repressor by preventing the binding of the RNA‐polymeras to the 6HDNO promoter.
